clinical_notes: 58-year-old male with Type 2 diabetes for 12 years. HbA1c 6.8%. No visible retinal lesions. Fundus appears normal with clear optic disc margins and healthy vasculature.
treatment: Continue current diabetes management. Annual screening recommended.
validated_report: No evidence of diabetic retinopathy. Retinal vasculature appears normal. Optic disc and macula are unremarkable. Recommend annual fundus screening.

clinical_notes: 45-year-old female with Type 2 diabetes for 8 years. HbA1c 7.5%. A few scattered microaneurysms visible in the temporal region. No hemorrhages or exudates.
treatment: Optimize glycemic control. Repeat screening in 12 months.
validated_report: Mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy detected. Scattered microaneurysms observed in the temporal quadrant. No hard exudates, hemorrhages, or neovascularization. Recommend glycemic optimization and 12-month follow-up.

clinical_notes: 62-year-old male with Type 2 diabetes for 18 years. HbA1c 8.9%. Multiple microaneurysms and dot-blot hemorrhages in all quadrants. Scattered hard exudates near the macula.
treatment: Urgent referral to ophthalmologist. Intensify glycemic control. Re-screen in 3–6 months.
validated_report: Moderate non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. Microaneurysms and dot-blot hemorrhages are present in multiple quadrants. Hard exudates observed near the macula, raising concern for clinically significant macular edema. Urgent ophthalmology referral recommended.

clinical_notes: 50-year-old female with Type 1 diabetes for 25 years. HbA1c 8.2%. Moderate number of microaneurysms and intraretinal hemorrhages. No exudates or cotton wool spots.
treatment: Ophthalmology referral within 4 weeks. Review diabetes management plan.
validated_report: Moderate non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. Intraretinal hemorrhages and microaneurysms distributed across multiple quadrants. No signs of proliferative changes. Recommend ophthalmology evaluation within one month.

clinical_notes: 67-year-old male with Type 2 diabetes for 22 years. HbA1c 9.4%. Extensive intraretinal hemorrhages in all four quadrants. Cotton wool spots and venous beading observed. No neovascularization yet.
treatment: Immediate ophthalmology referral. Consider pan-retinal photocoagulation. Aggressive blood sugar and blood pressure management.
validated_report: Severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. Meets 4-2-1 rule criteria with hemorrhages in all four quadrants and venous beading. Cotton wool spots present. High risk of progression to proliferative DR. Immediate referral for possible pan-retinal photocoagulation.

clinical_notes: 55-year-old female with uncontrolled Type 2 diabetes. HbA1c 10.1%. Intraretinal microvascular abnormalities (IRMA) in the nasal region. Multiple cotton wool spots and flame hemorrhages.
treatment: Urgent ophthalmology referral for laser therapy evaluation. Diabetes education and medication adjustment.
validated_report: Severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy with high-risk features. IRMA, cotton wool spots, and extensive flame hemorrhages indicate imminent risk of proliferative conversion. Urgent laser therapy evaluation required.

clinical_notes: 70-year-old male with Type 2 diabetes for 30 years. HbA1c 9.8%. Active neovascularization at the disc (NVD) and elsewhere (NVE). Vitreous hemorrhage in the right eye. Tractional retinal detachment suspected.
treatment: Emergency ophthalmology referral. Pan-retinal photocoagulation or anti-VEGF injections. Possible vitrectomy if tractional detachment confirmed.
validated_report: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy with high-risk characteristics. Active neovascularization at the disc and elsewhere with vitreous hemorrhage. Possible tractional retinal detachment. Emergency intervention with anti-VEGF therapy and/or pan-retinal photocoagulation is indicated. Vitrectomy may be necessary.

clinical_notes: 63-year-old female with Type 1 diabetes for 35 years. HbA1c 8.7%. Florid neovascularization with fibrous proliferation. Pre-retinal hemorrhage observed. Previous pan-retinal photocoagulation scars present.
treatment: Anti-VEGF injections. Evaluate for additional laser treatment. Close follow-up every 2–4 weeks.
validated_report: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy with fibrous proliferation despite prior pan-retinal photocoagulation. Active neovascularization and pre-retinal hemorrhage indicate disease progression. Anti-VEGF therapy recommended with frequent monitoring.

clinical_notes: 40-year-old male with newly diagnosed Type 2 diabetes. HbA1c 7.2%. Single microaneurysm in the temporal arcade region. Otherwise normal fundus.
treatment: Lifestyle modification. Repeat fundus screening in 12 months.
validated_report: Mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. Isolated microaneurysm detected in the temporal arcade. No other retinal abnormalities. Recommend lifestyle modifications, glycemic optimization, and annual follow-up screening.

clinical_notes: 52-year-old female with Type 2 diabetes for 5 years. HbA1c 6.5%. Well-controlled diabetes. Normal fundus examination with no retinal lesions detected.
validated_report: No diabetic retinopathy detected. Fundus examination is normal. Patient's diabetes is well-controlled. Continue current treatment plan and schedule annual retinal screening.
